tracks.legalName: Expungement of Records of Arrests and Charges Not Resulting in Conviction (N.J.S.A. 2C:52-6)
tracks.publicName: Expunge a New Jersey arrest that did not lead to a conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Records of an arrest, charge and related proceedings that did not result in conviction may be expunged at any time, with no waiting period. Where the case was dismissed or the person was acquitted on all counts, New Jersey Courts states that the court can order an immediate expungement. There is no filing fee. Expungement in New Jersey is defined at N.J.S.A. 2C:52-1 as the extraction and isolation of criminal justice records, not their destruction. In most contexts the person may then answer that the event did not occur. Certain law enforcement, judicial and specified licensing uses survive under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-27. The relief reaches New Jersey records only: federal and out-of-state records are untouched, although out-of-state convictions still count when assessing eligibility. There is no federal immigration effect.

exclusions: Title 39 motor vehicle matters, including DWI. N.J.S.A. 2C:52-28 puts the whole chapter outside them.
Federal, out-of-state and tribal records.
A dismissal following completion of a supervisory treatment or diversion programme, which is treated differently and interacts with the one-time-only rules elsewhere in the chapter.

The Judiciary kit tells filers to leave the signature line blank for the judge and to leave the monies-owed section for the court.

How to order the New Jersey State Police State Bureau of Identification fingerprint-based criminal history, and why it comes first: it produces the indictable and disorderly persons count that decides the route and the case identifiers the petition needs. Missing case identifiers are the leading cause of rejected petitions.

How to file. New Jersey Courts now directs self-represented filers to the eCourts Expungement System, which assembles the petition and order from entered data and states "It's free". LegalEase prepares the participant's answers and the case list so the entry is accurate; whether LegalEase produces paper on the Judiciary kit instead is a build decision recorded as an open question.

Who is served, the objection diary, and what happens next: if no agency objects the court may enter the order without a hearing under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-11; if there is an objection the court holds a hearing. The exact objection window is recorded as an open question and is not stated to the participant as a fixed number of days.

The step that decides whether the expungement actually works: after entry, a certified copy of the signed order must reach every agency holding records, built from the SBI history. An agency that is not served keeps its copy. Keep a certified copy of the order permanently, allow six to twelve months for State Police processing, and verify afterwards, including through the State Police expungement status portal.

tracks.publicName: Expunge a New Jersey felony conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: "Indictable offence" is New Jersey's word for a felony and is heard in Superior Court; "disorderly persons" and "petty disorderly persons" offences are the misdemeanour equivalents and are usually Municipal Court matters. An expungement application may be presented where the person has one crime conviction and no subsequent crime conviction; or one crime and no more than three disorderly persons or petty disorderly persons offences; or multiple convictions all listed in a single judgment of conviction; or multiple convictions that were interdependent or closely related in circumstances and committed as part of a sequence of events within a comparatively short period, regardless of the individual conviction or sentencing dates. The single-judgment and closely-related routes carry no numeric cap, which is the difference between a five-year petition and a ten-year Clean Slate petition for a participant with several convictions from one episode. The ordinary waiting period is five years from the latest of the most recent conviction, payment of any court-ordered financial assessment, satisfactory completion of probation or parole, or release from incarceration. Expungement in New Jersey is defined at N.J.S.A. 2C:52-1 as the extraction and isolation of criminal justice records, not their destruction. In most contexts the person may then answer that the event did not occur. Certain law enforcement, judicial and specified licensing uses survive under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-27. The relief reaches New Jersey records only: federal and out-of-state records are untouched, although out-of-state convictions still count when assessing eligibility. There is no federal immigration effect.

exclusions: Any conviction on the non-expungeable lists at N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2(b) and (c), which cover criminal homicide other than certain death by auto, kidnapping, luring and enticing, human trafficking, aggravated sexual assault and sexual assault and most sex offences, endangering the welfare of a child by sexual conduct, robbery, arson, perjury and false swearing, offences against public officials or government, official misconduct and bribery and public corruption by a public officer or employee, and drug distribution above the statutory thresholds. A further petition after a previous criminal conviction expungement, barred by N.J.S.A. 2C:52-14(e), except that Clean Slate remains available.

participantInputs.question: When did you finish probation or parole, or get released from custody, on each matter?

participantInputs.conditionDescription: Asked because that route carries no numeric cap.

participantInputs.question: Did any of these offences happen as part of one connected sequence of events over a short period?
participantInputs.conditionDescription: Asked because the interdependent-or-closely-related route also carries no numeric cap, and characterising it is where the largest eligibility payoff sits.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The review approved this track with limitations. Its staged proposal normalizes to a single official_pdf_fill route on the same reasoning as the arrest track: the classification and non-expungeable screen decide whether anything is generated, which is eligibility screening rather than a second output. The venue correction is confirmed: A5826, read at the New Jersey Legislature's own channel, amends N.J.S.2C:52-2 by striking "most recent conviction for a crime was" and inserting the residence-or-conviction-county rule, so the internal reference's "county of the most recent offense" is wrong and the review is right. tracks.legalName: Expungement of Disorderly Persons and Petty Disorderly Persons Offences (N.J.S.A. 2C:52-3)
tracks.publicName: Expunge New Jersey disorderly persons offences

controllingAuthority.summary: Available to a person convicted of one or more disorderly persons or petty disorderly persons offences who has not been convicted of any crime, in this State or any other jurisdiction; a person with any crime conviction uses N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2 instead. Three alternative routes: no more than five disorderly persons offences, no more than five petty disorderly persons offences, or a combination of no more than five; or multiple offences whose convictions were entered on the same day; or multiple offences that were interdependent or closely related in circumstances and committed as part of a sequence of events within a comparatively short period. The same-day and closely-related routes carry no numeric cap. The statute expressly provides that a person shall not be required to provide plea or sentencing transcripts or presentence reports with the application or any other filing. Expungement in New Jersey is defined at N.J.S.A. 2C:52-1 as the extraction and isolation of criminal justice records, not their destruction. In most contexts the person may then answer that the event did not occur. Certain law enforcement, judicial and specified licensing uses survive under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-27. The relief reaches New Jersey records only: federal and out-of-state records are untouched, although out-of-state convictions still count when assessing eligibility. There is no federal immigration effect.

exclusions: Any crime conviction anywhere, which moves the participant to the indictable track.
Title 39 motor vehicle matters, including DWI. N.J.S.A. 2C:52-28.
A further petition after a previous criminal conviction expungement, barred by N.J.S.A. 2C:52-14(e), except that Clean Slate remains available.

components.notes: The verified petition under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-7, from the New Jersey Judiciary kit "How to Expunge Your Criminal and/or Juvenile Record", CN 10557, retained in Edition 1.2 at REV-2020-06, which matches the June 2020 update that removed the filing fee. New Jersey Courts now directs self-represented filers to the eCourts Expungement System, which assembles the same documents from entered data. The early-pathway checkbox on Form A-Continued for this track is the three-year variant under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-3(b)(2), not the four-year indictable variant.
The statements N.J.S.A. 2C:52-8 requires with the petition, including the statement about prior expungements and the statement of financial assessments. Part of the same Judiciary kit.
The order for hearing under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-9, issued by the court. The participant prepares the draft; the court issues it.

The proposed expungement order under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-11, naming the State Police, the county prosecutor, the Superior and Municipal Courts, the arresting agency, probation and every other record-holding agency. The Judiciary kit tells filers to leave the signature line blank for the judge and to leave the monies-owed section for the court.

How to order the New Jersey State Police State Bureau of Identification fingerprint-based criminal history, and why it comes first: it produces the indictable and disorderly persons count that decides the route and the case identifiers the petition needs. Missing case identifiers are the leading cause of rejected petitions.

How to file. New Jersey Courts now directs self-represented filers to the eCourts Expungement System, which assembles the petition and order from entered data and states "It's free". LegalEase prepares the participant's answers and the case list so the entry is accurate; whether LegalEase produces paper on the Judiciary kit instead is a build decision recorded as an open question.

Who is served, the objection diary, and what happens next: if no agency objects the court may enter the order without a hearing under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-11; if there is an objection the court holds a hearing. The exact objection window is recorded as an open question and is not stated to the participant as a fixed number of days.

The step that decides whether the expungement actually works: after entry, a certified copy of the signed order must reach every agency holding records, built from the SBI history. An agency that is not served keeps its copy. Keep a certified copy of the order permanently, allow six to twelve months for State Police processing, and verify afterwards, including through the State Police expungement status portal.

That N.J.S.A. 2C:52-3 expressly provides the person shall not be required to provide plea or sentencing transcripts or presentence reports with the application or any other filing. This is directly useful to a participant who fears a document hunt, and the internal reference omits it.

That the cap on this track is five, not three: New Jersey Courts' self-help page states the one-indictable-plus-three-offences rule, which describes the indictable route, and a participant reading it may believe three is the cap for everything. The marijuana and paraphernalia regrading rules are applied to the count before it is taken.

tracks.publicName: Clear your whole New Jersey record after ten years

controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted of one or more crimes, one or more disorderly persons or petty disorderly persons offences, or any combination, who is not otherwise eligible under another section, may petition to expunge the entire record, unless the person has a conviction for a crime not subject to expungement under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2(b) or (c). The waiting period is ten years from the latest of the most recent conviction, payment of any court-ordered financial assessment, satisfactory completion of probation or parole, or release from incarceration. Where the ten-year period is otherwise satisfied but a financial assessment is unpaid for reasons other than willful noncompliance, the person may still apply and the balance is converted to a civil judgment transferred to the State Treasurer. The route is available notwithstanding the N.J.S.A. 2C:52-14(e) prior-expungement bar. No application may be filed under this section after the automated Clean Slate process is established. Expungement in New Jersey is defined at N.J.S.A. 2C:52-1 as the extraction and isolation of criminal justice records, not their destruction. In most contexts the person may then answer that the event did not occur. Certain law enforcement, judicial and specified licensing uses survive under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-27. The relief reaches New Jersey records only: federal and out-of-state records are untouched, although out-of-state convictions still count when assessing eligibility. There is no federal immigration effect.

exclusions: Any conviction for a crime not subject to expungement under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2(b) or (c). One such conviction defeats the track entirely.
A person who is otherwise eligible under another section. Whether "not otherwise eligible" is applied strictly is recorded below as an open question.
Title 39 motor vehicle matters, including DWI.
Federal, out-of-state and tribal records, which are not reachable but do count toward eligibility.

tracks.publicName: New Jersey's automatic record clearing, and where it stands

controllingAuthority.summary: The State shall develop and implement an automated process by which all convictions and related records are rendered inaccessible to the public, through sealing, expungement or an equivalent process, for a person convicted of one or more crimes or offences, unless the person has a conviction not subject to expungement under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2(b) or (c), upon the expiration of ten years. A task force was established to design it and reported in 2022. The process is not operational: Assembly Bill A5095, introduced May 14, 2026, states that it still does not exist and that eligible people must still file a petition with the court. The section also requires that a person's convictions and criminal history be restored in certain circumstances if the person is subsequently convicted of a crime not subject to expungement. Expungement in New Jersey is defined at N.J.S.A. 2C:52-1 as the extraction and isolation of criminal justice records, not their destruction. In most contexts the person may then answer that the event did not occur. Certain law enforcement, judicial and specified licensing uses survive under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-27. The relief reaches New Jersey records only: federal and out-of-state records are untouched, although out-of-state convictions still count when assessing eligibility. There is no federal immigration effect.

exclusions: Any conviction for a crime not subject to expungement under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2(b) or (c).
Everyone, for the time being. The process is not operational as of 2026-08-06 and nothing happens automatically.
